intended_object: The relative affine Euclidean height of x ∈ K^ι over a number field K: the Euclidean projective height of (1, x), i.e. ∏_{w|∞}(1+Σ|σ_w x_i|²)^{m_w/2}·∏_{v finite} max(1, max_i |x_i|_v). Inferred from the docstring and the module doc, which cites Evertse–Ferretti.
explanation: The definition applies arakelovMulHeight to the Option ι-indexed tuple with the value 1 at none and x_i at some i. This tuple is never zero, so the junk value for the zero tuple never applies. By arakelovMulHeight_eq, the value is ∏_w (Σ|σ_w y_i|²)^{m_w/2} · ∏ᶠ_v sup_i |y_i|_v with y = (1, x). Here m_w is 1 at real places and 2 at complex places, so a complex place contributes the squared complex absolute value, and the finite places use the normalized FinitePlace absolute values. This is the standard Euclidean affine height H_K(1, x) of Evertse–Ferretti, in its relative form as the docstring says. The supporting lemmas agree: the height is at least 1, its value at x = 0 is 1, and it is invariant under reindexing. The construction needs the number-field setting (its places, its degree and the product formula). Mathlib's Height.mulHeight uses the max norm at the archimedean places as well, so it is a different height, and Mathlib has no Euclidean version.
